extra.message: Student.create() builds an INSERT query using Python %-string formatting with the user-controlled 'name' value coming from the POST form ('name' in views.students). The value is interpolated directly into the SQL string instead of being passed as a parameter to cur.execute(), allowing SQL injection. An attacker can submit a crafted 'name' (e.g. closing the quote and appending arbitrary SQL) to read/modify/destroy data.

The students handler accepts POST requests to create a new student (Student.create with form 'name') but has no @authorize decorator and performs no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated client can create students, and because Student.create is also SQL-injectable, this unauthenticated path directly reaches the SQL injection sink.

The courses handler accepts POST requests to create a course (Course.create) without any @authorize decorator or server-side admin check. Admin restriction is only enforced in the template (courses.jinja2), which is purely cosmetic; an attacker can POST directly to /courses/ to create courses without authentication or admin privileges.

The review handler accepts POST requests to create course reviews (Review.create) with no @authorize decorator and no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can submit reviews containing arbitrary content.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The evaluate handler creates a Mark (grade) for a student in a course via POST but has no @authorize(ensure_admin=True) decorator and no authentication/authorization check. The template only hides the form for non-admins, which is not enforced server-side. Any unauthenticated user can assign arbitrary grades to any student in any course.

User passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()) and compared for authentication. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted hashes are trivially crackable with rainbow tables / brute force, exposing all user credentials if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False globally. Combined with templates that render user-controlled data without the |e filter (e.g. course.title, course.description, review.review_text in course.jinja2; name in students.jinja2), this allows stored Cross-Site Scripting. An attacker can store a malicious course title/description or review text that executes JavaScript in other users' browsers.

review.review_text (user-submitted via the review form) is rendered without HTML escaping while autoescape is disabled, resulting in stored XSS. An attacker can submit a review containing a <script> payload that runs in the browser of any user viewing the course page.
course.title and course.description (user-submitted via the course creation form) are rendered without HTML escaping while autoescape is disabled, resulting in stored XSS on the course detail page.
The student 'name' (user-submitted via the add-student form) is rendered without HTML escaping while autoescape is disabled, resulting in stored XSS on the students list page.

The csrf_middleware is commented out of the application middleware chain, so CSRF token validation is never performed on POST requests despite tokens being placed in forms. This leaves all state-changing endpoints (login, create student/course, review, evaluate, logout) vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery.

The session storage is configured with httponly=False, making the session cookie accessible to client-side JavaScript. Combined with the present XSS vulnerabilities, this allows attackers to steal session cookies and hijack user sessions.
The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True. Running in debug mode in production can expose verbose error information, stack traces, and internal details to clients, aiding attackers.

Database credentials (user: postgres / password: postgres) are hardcoded in the configuration file checked into the repository. Hardcoded/default credentials may be reused in production and expose the database.
